title: Episodic and Semantic Memory

features: SQLite restart persistence and integrity checks

persistence_and_restart.atomicity: SQLite transaction boundaries use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for add, supersede, and delete.
persistence_and_restart.recovery: Strict record/content-hash/provenance/event decoding and PRAGMA integrity_check fail closed on corruption.
persistence_and_restart.deletion: Deletion is an audited state transition; deleted rows remain available to owner-scoped history but are excluded from search.

security_and_negative_results.authorization: Every get/search/history/update/supersede/delete operation requires owner and project scope; missing rows do not disclose other scopes.
security_and_negative_results.admission: No write path accepts absent or mismatched intent/provenance; model proposals require approval.
security_and_negative_results.provenance: Every record has source kind, source ID, actor, approval state, timestamp, metadata, and content SHA-256.
security_and_negative_results.network: No network, cloud inference, telemetry, or remote upload was added.

metrics.search_algorithm: deterministic lexical token scoring; no semantic embedding quality claim

limitations: The backend is a deterministic lexical baseline; a local vector/semantic backend requires a separately measured A/B phase.

The existing Zetsu repository-agent registry remains stale relative to the current v2 checkout; G2 implementation and tests were performed locally after the deterministic promotion-target failure recorded in G1.
The socket-concurrency regression requires host socket permission because the restricted shell denies socket creation; the unchanged test passed under that permission.
The full G0 production certification was not repeated, per the roadmap instruction and G1 certification; the selected previous-phase regression was run.

rollback_target.description: G1-certified shared core without the G2 memory service; production/v1 remains separately immutable.
